item.title: City of normacy: Re: City of normacy
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

The Foundations discovers an area that negates anomalous effects and memories or instructions relating to the anomalous

This is always a little tricky because it implies 'all anomalous effects work in the same way' which is weird because like…why do memetic effects, teleporting humans and replicating cake all work in the same way?

Forgetting about anomalous stuff in general feels weird too; like, it feels perhaps like this being a generic antimemetic thing that makes you forget about it would be a good way to keep the core of this without getting rid of all the narrative building off it?

Though this brings us onto the narrative: the first paragraph feels very promising; the effects expanding and the foundation struggling to handle the situation is a really great start. This comes crashing down when it turns into it really being focussed on 'what does the anomaly do' later on which feels…underwhelming? My advice is figure out a whole narrative arc from a beginning of 'the foundation doesn't understand it' to an ending where they manage to come up with some kind of containment that's some sort of horrible compromise.

I'm kinda…iffy on the anomalous human at the centre of this: it could be a good idea but it doesn't really feel like your summary hints at why it's important? It just kinda feels like there's a person at the centre, rather than all of the effects boiling down to being like…the persons guilt at hurting their family by reality bending and them trying to force anomalous behaviour to not work ever to protect everyone else, y'know?

item.title: SCP Idea: "Fuck Stairs, I've Got Whiteboards!": Re: SCP-5632 Idea: A Word, if you will, about your transphobic B U L L S H I T
item.content:encoded:
This was created by an "anartist" who is all about practical stuff. Would probably involve exploration of Whiteboard Dimension to her old notes and such.

So, tell me about this: what do her old notes say? Why are they of interest now? What's in the whiteboard dimension that makes it interesting to explore?

I think my concern with this idea is that it's what I'd term 'overbroad': it's the kinda idea that opens you up to all kinds of cool and interesting things you could do with it, which in turn means finding the one that's actually interesting is really hard.

I like the idea of tying an anartist in here; and like, exploring what she got up to using this and stuff, but my largest concern is really just that I don't have a good idea of where this goes or anything. The actual whiteboard might be a touch overcomplex in how it works: it feels like it could be streamlined to have more focus with a few less anomalous bits to it but I don't think this is necessarily a huge issue as long as you do something interesting with it.

item.title: Deus Comedenti (Translation: God Eater): Re: Deus Comedenti (Translation: God Eater)
item.content:encoded:
+ show block
– hide block

Something that bugs me about this concept is that it seems to be including widespread murder of homeless or prisoners merely for an easy excuse to have a moral dilemma. That seems excessively grimdark for the sake of easy horror - "over the top" in terms of violence just for the sake of "isn't that scary?"

I'm also not full convinced on the whole this machine was built to eat gods but now it eats humans and also that anything that was designed WAY back in prehistory to kill gods wouldn't be likely to convert them into electricity.

Moreover, I think you're still missing a narrative arc here. What is the story about? Just a discussion of this magical god killing machine and its history, isn't really a story. Neither is just presenting a dilemma like "Should the government be sacrificing the poor for benefit of the rich?" (which is btw what you're saying)

Narratives need more than a dilemma. Where is the conflict? Characters? plot, etc?


I think you should consider these things, and if you don't want to change the proposal, consider reaching out to other reviewers to see if maybe its just me.

item.title: The Perpetual Lawnmower: The Perpetual Lawnmower
item.content:encoded:
Seeking greenlight.
SCP Article.

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a lawnmower that perpetually gets faster and doesn't suffer from wind resistance or interact with physical objects, until it comes into contact with grass. When it touches grass it becomes 'real' and suffers the effects of wind resistance from the speed that it is going.

Central Narrative: This is an anomaly created by a new POI, who created this specifically to mow their lawn for them without any effort. This SCP was found moving away from this POI's place of residence at very high speeds, allowing the foundation to get a rough idea to where this POI lives.

item.title: SCP concept-The ring of mimicry: Re: SCP concept-The ring of mimicry
item.content:encoded:
Why does it exist? , the foundation doesn't have a lot of information on the origins of this ring, however, it can be theorized on what it was used for. The box transformed by the ring only attacks objects who come in close to it, non organic objects inside of the container are fine while organic tissue is slowly dissolved, and it can be easily deactivated by removing the ring from its container. it was probably created to guard valuables. The ring doesn't function well though, it doesn't stop converting containers automatically, the ring only stops when taken out of its container which would make this very troublesome for extended use.

How was it used? I kinda answered that in why it exists, it was most likely used to defend valuables, even though it didn't work well for that purpose.

How is it being used now? the scp is currently being contained via actively moving it between boxes as to prevent SCP-XXXX-1 from even manifesting.

I feel as if my wording here wasn't precise and clear, my draft on this could probably do it more justice.

Overall, thank you for your critique, Im thinking more about the narrative and origins of the scp than I did before, if I wanted to, I could put much more into its story but I kind of want to keep it simple so Ill be experimenting with this.

item.title: Singularity - Seeking Greenlight (2/2): Re: Singularity - Seeking Greenlight (2/2)
item.content:encoded:
Got a PM about this, took a look. I'll admit that I'm kind of immediately skeptical about the plot setup, especially since the initial manifestation of the anomaly is so sudden and abrupt, as well as unusually conveniently focused on a Foundation personnel member who just happens to be the almost contrivedly perfect model of guilt you need for a main character.

+ show block
– hide block

A mysterious black, metal object resembling an hourglass appears in the sky above a foundation site and crashes through the roof.

I admit that I personally found this kind of silly. Out of all the places and buildings this object could have appeared over and crashed into, it just happens to be a Foundation site that just happened have a guy who would want to research it? No one found it suspicious that the thing crashed near a guy who could research it? No foul play or mind-affecting anomaly was suspected?

appears to consume the time of living beings near it, causing them to leap forward in time and age accordingly.

As an aside for the draft, you're going to need to describe the anomaly in terms that don't seem like they're out of a D&D manual or fantasy videogame lorebook. A Foundation researcher looking at this would use the description "reality-changing temporal anomaly", not "it consumes people's time".

The object ends up killing several researchers, but one seems to be unaffected

This in itself already kind of sets up your main character as Mary Sue-ish. Not only does the guy survive the incident that killed several of his (presumably close in physical and mental makeup as he is, being all humans?) coworkers, he's also unaffected entirely? I'd find this more believable and more heart-wrenching if there were multiple initial survivors, but this guy happened to be the least harmed by the anomaly.

After the anomaly is contained, the research wants to learn more about it, and is appointed head researcher.

Again, Mary Sue/author meddling contrived plot vibes for me. The guy who just happens to remain unaffected later just happens to be at the site where the thing crashes, and just happens to have the credentials, resources, and space in his schedule be appointed head researcher of the thing? And also just happens to want to research the item in the first place?

Later, the SCP permanently attaches itself to him. Through interviews with Dr. Glass,

Given how often Glass is mentioned already in existing works, I personally would recommend using a different character/make up your own name for the psychologist/counselor/therapist/etc.. The plot is already rather contrived enough; having an often-namedropped character from the very start of the SCP wiki's tales happen to be the one to interview the guy seems gratuitous.

we learn he is suffering from survivor’s guilt and isolation. During subsequent testing, we find out that the SCP can allow the researcher to exist outside of time. (Time stop) The end of the arc will have the researcher coming to terms with the conflict he feels towards the SCP being attached to him and using it to help the foundation/the world, while leaving the origin and purpose of the SCP open ended.

I'd make the guy more conflicted. What you have currently runs the risk of the same sort of superhero origin story as lots of existing popular media franchise characters (Peter Parker from Spider-Man, for example. Guy loses his uncle, has powers now, goes on to help the world in spite of guilt).

Maybe have the guy start out as repeatedly denying fault, but still making sure that he and the anomaly are properly contained. Have him request counseling because that's proper protocol, but then waste the first few sessions because he's reluctant to admit blame. Have him gradually realize what he's done because of the lives that have been lost, and how he needs to be more mindful of those around him moving forward. Don't have him just eventually come to terms with the situation and become superhero-esque to help the Foundation/world, have scientists approach him with a request for further testing, and have him only accept with their full consent and awareness of his anomaly file and psychological reports.

I’m hoping to expand on the backstory of the SCP in future tales or articles, as well as feature the researcher in some of my future articles. While I couldn’t explain every detail here, I have the main arc of the story pretty well thought out.

I personally recommend not relying too much on future works if it means delaying a lot of the actually potentially good material in the page that's supposed to introduce the character and their anomaly. You want the article to tell a story that the audience will be invested in, beyond just setting up scaffolding for your personal anomaly-powered OC (does he really need the timestop ability to tell
a good story?). Right now what you have here seems kind of bland—it's just "guy happens to be messed up by anomaly, guy overcomes it, also has timestop now".

I'm also iffy on the guy being inserted into future articles given that in-universe he should be just kept in his own containment and not frivolously crosstested. If you really want to build a lot of lore around him, I'd recommend focusing on the tales, where the structure is looser and the threshold for suspension of disbelief is a bit more generous.

I’d also like to show that it was no accident the anomaly bonded to this researcher.

So why did the anomaly "bond" to this guy? Why not include this in the article about the guy and his anomaly?

You've already gotten your two greenlights, so it's entirely possible that you don't need to incorporate edits from my response for readers to enjoy the piece. I personally am still not quite sold on either the plot or the main character; however, remember that I am extremely picky when it comes to character-centric pieces like this. Since the anomaly is kind of generic so far as effects go, the success of the article will hinge on the character being someone the audience can both believe in as a person and relate to as an individual. I myself am not quite convinced as of yet.

No greenlight from me, but I wish you the best of luck with the drafting.

item.title: SCP concept-The ring of mimicry: Re: SCP concept-The ring of mimicry
item.content:encoded:
+ Cope Crit
- Close

Okay, here we go my man….

The ring, while easy to contain, can be catastrophic if not watched after. It does not have a size limit on what it can animate. That means, if given time, the ring could animate the entire facility (key word is given time, it would take decades for the ring to achieve that). Thus the ring has many re-containment procedures and fail-safes to prevent that.

Okay, this sounds like it needs to go into the Elevator Pitch. This is just more (well detailed) notes on the object. But this also leads me to ask WHY does the ring do this? Was it created? Did it just appear from nowhere?

Hook/Attention-Grabber: For this idea, I tried to turn the whole box idea on its head. The whole "if you put it in a box and it stays there, then its safe", I thought about if you put it in a box and then the box tried to kill you, what would it be?

I will not lie, this is a interesting concept. HOWEVER, I'm still concerned with the narrative. So I have three simple questions for you. Why does it exist? How was it used? How is it being used now?

Why does it exist? Did it come from another dimension or did magic create it? Maybe something else entirely…

How was it used? If someone created it, was it to replace a stolen item, or maybe to mimic something they couldn't have?

How is it being used now? Okay… The box is trying to kill us? How do we contain the box? Unless someone else has it…

Overall, I think this is a very interesting concept that lacks narrative. Get that figured out and I'm sure this will do well. Can't wait to see where this idea goes.

- Close

item.title: Pep-Talk Sticky Notes: Re: Pep-Talk Sticky Notes
item.content:encoded:
+ Cope Crit
- Close

Okay, here we go… Let's go over this, shall we?

A sticky note pad that is only useable by personnel currently experiencing negative emotions. When said personnel take one, the message on the note viewable only to them calms them down and leaves them feeling content for a period of three minutes afterward. When the three minutes are up, the subject is left in a neutral state. The messages are reported as upbeat and encouraging.

Why does the sticky pad do this? So far (in my eyes), it seems like a dumbed-down version of SCP-999. Other then encouraging people, is there anything else?

It logs how the anomaly is used during testing and ends with a log in which the notepad manifests a secondary anomalous property. It also logs the potential uses of the notepad.

This is not a Central Narrative. This would be put into Page Layout.

I plan the Containment Procedures to be attention-grabbing, with them going something like As SCP-XXXX poses no threat to the security and safety of Site-XX and its personnel, SCP-XXXX is allowed to be freely used whenever it manifests contained in a lock-protected drawer in Dr. XXXXX's office. Also, I plan to put an interview log in which the notepad manifests in the middle of a stressful interview and then manifests to the interviewee after failing the interview miserably.

This would also be in Page Layout. Also, could you expand on what you mean by "manifests"? Can it turn into something else. Also, Also, an interview? For who? Why? How would it correlate to your current idea. Can the sticky pad talk?

I know it's another item SCP, but they work best for my writing style. Also, I want to write this one to be easy to understand for people who have never read an SCP before.

Nothing is wrong with another item SCP. We have plenty of them and continue to have plenty of them. The key is making them new and unique with a different direction. So far, you haven't gone indepth with the SCP. I suggest you think more about the SCP. Read a few guides. They always help me. You can also seek help from the butterfly squad. They're always ready to help and much more experienced then myself.

http://www.scpwiki.com/guide-hub
http://www.scpwiki.com/butterfly-squad-roster

If you want to bounce ideas with me, I'd be more than happen to help you. You can PM me anytime.

- Close

item.title: Hive-Mind Wolves: Hive-Mind Wolves
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Large Special Containment Procedures and Description, as well as a brief addendum, and a video transcript.

Elevator Pitch: A group of three wolves that can see through opaque objects, but cannot see through transparent/translucent objects at all, any person seen by an instance can be elevated into a hostile, collective hive mind, however it has a limited range.

Central Narrative: These wolves can turn entire groups of people into collective hive minds, that are violent, and can cause mass destruction, people can be initiated into the hive mind almost instantly, but it takes 15 minutes out of sight of the instances to exit, requiring some pretty specific methods and tactics to prevent the hive mind from simply walking back into the SCP's line of sight, or allowing the SCP to breach containment entirely.

However, the SCP instances and the members of the hive minds appear to want to destroy the foundation, as those affected have been seen to destroy foundation buildings and locations before they would be held off.

It would be found somewhere in washington after attracting the attention of the foundation as a horde of people started raiding a foundation building, and started to essentialy dismantle and destroy it, before those people would be either kept away by task forces or neutralized to keep away if necessary. Several groups would have to get together to contain the SCP and lock it away in Area-14, in Nevada.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Just the pure speculation of the damage this SCP could do, due to it's ability to turn large masses of people into essentially their own weapon, while maintaining their individual intelligence such as ability to use weaponry and vehicles, as well as that the SCP and the hive minds appear to have a hatred or distaste for The Foundation, and seek to destroy or dismantle it.

Additional Notes: Nothing else much to say here, except, thank you for looking over this, and giving me your critique, and I'll do my best to pay attention.
